header.name: Distributed Systems
header.description: This objective of this course is to train students in understanding fundamental concepts of distributed systems as well as develop the ability to design and implement distributed systems. The course will also cover a number of case studies of real world distributed systems  such as MapReduce/Hadoop, Hadoop File System, BitTorrent, Amazon Dynamo. For each case study, various design decisions and corresponding tradeoffs will be critiqued. The course will require and instill system programming skills.
prerequisites_mandatory: Students must have good programming skills with at least one of the following languages: Java, Scala, Go, Python.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students shall understand the fundamental concepts of of distributed systems such as consistency, availability, scalability, fault tolerance, concurrency and communication.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students shall understand some important algorithms for consensus and election and how they are employed in large scale distributed systems (including various cloud platforms).

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to develop distributed applications using communication libraries/frameworks such as RPC, ZeroMQ, RabbitMQ.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to analyze and critique real world systems (such as Apache Hadoop and Amazon Dynamo) in terms of how these systems are being used to solve compute and data intensive problems (such as storing large amounts of data, building a index for web search engines)

lecture_topics: Coordination: Clock synchronization, logical clocks, vector clocks
Leader Election, Consensus and Fault Tolerance (Zookeeper, Raft, Paxos, etc.)
Distributed File Systems: Hadoop File System (HDFS) / Google File System (GFS)
Distributed Computation: MapReduce, Hadoop and Spark
Peer-to-Peer Systems: BitTorrent and Distributed Hash Tables
Transactions, Concurrency control and Recovery (Two Phase Commit, Chandy-Lamport’s Distributed Snapshots)
Distributed databases and key-value stores: Amazon Dynamo / Google Spanner
Resource Scheduling and Management: Google Borg and Kubernetes

resources.title: Distributed Systems by Tannenbaum and Van Steen, 3rd Edition and Distributed Systems: Concepts and Design by Coulouris et al, 5th edition, Pearson
Virtual Machines: Versatile Platforms for Systems and Processes. (Morgan Kaufmann. 2005) By Jim Smith and Ravi Nair

Proceeding of IEEE/ACM transactions and conferences, e.g. OSDI, NSDI, SOSP, EuroSys etc. on Distributed Systems and related areas All the papers will be made available by the instructor and posted on course website.
